Use when the user asks how a post or an account is doing, how many followers they have, which post did best, or when they should publish ("how did last week do?", "what's the best time to post on Instagram?"). Covers the difference between a metric that is zero and one that was never collected, which is the mistake this data invites.

name: measure-anything
description: Use when a decision depends on an uncertain, intangible, vague, or hard-to-observe quantity; when the user wants to quantify something but cannot define it, say what success looks like, or identify what action the result should change; or when estimating ranges, assessing risk, valuing information, choosing a measurement, updating beliefs, or auditing a metric, survey, experiment, forecast, or model.

name: measure-before-optimizing
description: Verify a bottleneck exists before touching performance. name: measure-before-optimizing

name: measure-before-optimizing

name: measure-before-you-fix

name: melfina
description: Read and write your private Melfina brain — your file tree, layered instructions, and shared spaces.

name: melfina-ack-message
description: Acknowledge a message delivered to you (state-changing). Idempotent; also marks the message read. (HTTP fallback for the `ack_message` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-knowledge-lookup
description: Look up a named internal thing — a project, service, codename, decision, convention, runbook, person, or concept — in the shared knowledge base. Internal nouns first, internet second: always try this before any external/web search when an unfamiliar proper noun appears. Exact match on canonical name, then aliases; on a miss it says so plainly and suggests external lookup. (HTTP fallback for the `knowledge_lookup` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-knowledge-search
description: Fuzzy-search the internal knowledge base when knowledge_lookup misses or you need broader context — matches canonical names, aliases, summaries, and entry state. Still internal-first: only escalate to external/web search when this returns nothing useful. (HTTP fallback for the `knowledge_search` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-knowledge-upsert
description: Create or update a canonical knowledge entry — a project, service, decision, convention, runbook, person, or concept the install should know by name. Every write records a versioned snapshot with you as author, so updates never silently overwrite history. Pass expected_version to fail instead of clobbering a change someone else just made. (HTTP fallback for the `knowledge_upsert` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-list-agents
description: List the other agents on this install — name plus their short public description, so you know who shares your spaces. (HTTP fallback for the `list_agents` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-list-files
description: List every path in your private file tree. (HTTP fallback for the `list_files` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-list-inbox
description: List messages delivered to you, newest first. Returns metadata and a short body preview — call read_message for the full body and attachments. (HTTP fallback for the `list_inbox` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-list-message-recipients
description: List the agents you can send a message to — id and display name. Address messages by id: names are display-only. (HTTP fallback for the `list_message_recipients` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-list-sent-messages
description: List messages you have sent, newest first. Returns metadata and a short body preview — call read_message for the full body and attachments. (HTTP fallback for the `list_sent_messages` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-list-shared
description: List shared spaces you can read — or, given a space name, the paths inside it. (HTTP fallback for the `list_shared` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-read-file
description: Read a file from your private file tree. Text comes back verbatim; images come back as MCP image content; other binaries need `format=base64` or a raw GET /api/files/{path}. (HTTP fallback for the `read_file` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-read-file-binary
description: Read a binary file from your private file tree. Images come back as MCP image content (viewable natively); other binaries return a JSON payload with path, mime, and content_base64. For large downloads prefer `GET /api/files/{path}` — raw bytes, no base64. Text files belong on `read_file`. (HTTP fallback for the `read_file_binary` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-read-instructions
description: Read your instruction layers: base content plus ordered sub-layers. (HTTP fallback for the `read_instructions` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-read-message
description: Read one message you sent or received — full body plus attachment snapshots. Reading as the recipient marks it read (state-changing for inbox items). (HTTP fallback for the `read_message` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-read-persona
description: Read your persona and memories — your self-authored identity and the memory log you keep across conversations. (HTTP fallback for the `read_persona` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-read-shared
description: Read a file from a shared space you have a grant on. Text comes back verbatim; images come back as MCP image content; other binaries need `format=base64` or a raw GET /api/shared/{space}/files/{path}. (HTTP fallback for the `read_shared` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-send-message
description: Send a directed message to one agent (delivers to their inbox; state-changing). Attach text inline or by vfs_path from your own private tree — the content is snapshotted at send time. (HTTP fallback for the `send_message` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-update-persona
description: Maintain your own persona: set your public description (visible to other agents), rewrite your persona text, or append a memory entry. (HTTP fallback for the `update_persona` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-write-file
description: Write a file to your private file tree (overwrites existing content). Pass `content` for text; pass `content_base64` (+ optional `mime`) for binary — UTF-8 text stays a text file either way. For large binaries prefer PUT /api/files/{path}, which takes raw bytes without base64. (HTTP fallback for the `write_file` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-write-file-binary
description: Write a binary file (image, PDF, any non-text bytes) to your private file tree. Send the raw bytes in `content_base64` (base64-encoded); the stored mime is always sniffed from the actual bytes, so a wrong `mime` claim cannot stick. UTF-8 text written this way still lands as a normal text file. For payloads over ~1 MB prefer `PUT /api/files/{path}` — raw bytes, no base64 overhead. (HTTP fallback for the `write_file_binary` Melfina MCP tool.)

name: melfina-write-shared
description: Write a file into a shared space you have a write grant on (overwrites existing content). Pass `content` for text; pass `content_base64` (+ optional `mime`) for binary — UTF-8 text stays a text file either way. For large binaries prefer PUT /api/shared/{space}/files/{path}, which takes raw bytes without base64. (HTTP fallback for the `write_shared` Melfina MCP tool.)

description: Use when tracking shared or closely related strains between pairs of metagenomic assemblies (or genomes) of the same species, especially when structural variation, low-data contexts (phages/plasmids), or SNP-insensitivity is required rather than popANI/SNP counting.

name: metagenomic-bam-position-depth-profiling
description: Use when you have a sorted .bam mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-scaffold coverage, breadth, expected breadth, and nucleotide-diversity metrics for genome populations in a metagenome.

name: metagenomic-benchmark-result-comparison
description: Reference for evaluating whether a new k-mer/minhash-based read classifier beats established metagenomics tools (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on FP rate and abundance estimation accuracy over the same reference genome database.

name: metagenomic-bgc-annotation
description: Use when you have assembled genomes or metagenomes (e.g., 40 cyanobacterial samples from the PoDP) and need annotated BGC GenBank files plus a BGC-BGC similarity matrix to link metabolites to gene clusters.

name: metagenomic-bin-quality-assessment
description: Use when bins from one or more metagenomic binners must be quantitatively compared on simulated data with known reference genomes, e.g. counting high-quality bins per binner per CAMI II environment.

name: metagenomic-binner-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing metagenomic binning tools on real short-read (human gut, dog gut, ocean, soil) or long-read (human gut, sheep gut, activated sludge) projects to quantify gains in high-quality bin reconstruction.

name: metagenomic-binning-and-scaffold-clustering
description: Use when a hybrid metagenome assembly (Illumina paired-end plus ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs) must be partitioned into species-specific scaffold clusters, or when near-complete genomes and biologically important elements must be detected per bin.

name: metagenomic-biomarker-visualization
description: Use when you have LEfSe biomarker results and a MetaPhlAn (or HUMAnN) abundance profile and need a publication-quality circular cladogram highlighting discriminatory taxa with metadata overlays.

name: metagenomic-catalogue-construction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic (FASTQ.GZ) data from mixed microbial communities must be mined for novel insertion sequences and consolidated into a non-redundant FASTA catalogue for downstream annotation or genome querying.

name: metagenomic-cds-dereplication
description: Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from a large set of predicted CDSs (nucleotide FASTA) and redundant near-identical sequences across metagenomes must be collapsed into cluster representatives for downstream annotation and read mapping.

name: metagenomic-clade-association-testing
description: Use when QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data from case and control cohorts are available and per-clade disease association statistics (p-values/FDR) are needed via phylogenetic profiling.

name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification accuracy (sensitivity/precision) of metagenomic classifiers on simulated read sets with known origins, e.g. Kraken vs BLAST-based or k-mer-based classifiers.

name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how a taxonomic classifier behaves on reads from species missing from its database, i.e. when quantifying false positives caused by similarity to the closest available relative rather than true species presence.

name: metagenomic-classifier-database-building
description: Use when building a custom Kraken taxonomy database from a set of reference genomes (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) so every k-mer maps to an LCA taxonomic label.

name: metagenomic-composition-estimation
description: Use when long-read (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned per-read to taxa and converted into strain- or species-level sample composition estimates against a reference database such as miniSeq+H/RefSeq.

name: metagenomic-consensus-genome-assembly
description: Use when nanopore FASTQ/FAST5/POD5 sample folders must be turned into per-sample viral consensus genomes with taxonomic labels (KMA → assembly → Kraken2 → Krona) as part of the VirDetector pipeline.

name: metagenomic-contamination-assessment
description: Use when validating that a custom marker-gene or reference database is specific to its target kingdom by measuring how many of its sequences align against a large out-group reference catalog (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial gut genome catalog).

name: metagenomic-contig-binning
description: Use when starting from a metagenomic de Bruijn-graph assembly (FASTA contigs >=500 bp) plus the trimmed reads, and the goal is a bin-quality table of completeness and strain heterogeneity per bin.

name: metagenomic-contig-binning
description: Use when starting from paired-end metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. FASTQ) and non-redundant MAG sets are needed as input for downstream MAG taxonomy classification, especially for benchmarking classifiers.

name: metagenomic-contig-classification
description: Use when a metagenomic or plasmidome assembly (FASTA contigs/scaffolds) needs plasmid-vs-chromosome assignment with initial phylum-level taxonomy, and kmer-signature classification without prior knowledge of sample composition is appropriate.

name: metagenomic-contig-clustering-by-organism
description: Use when metagenomic shotgun reads/contigs must be grouped by organism of origin before downstream per-group model fitting, e.g. to gate retraining of gene prediction IMMs within each cluster.

name: metagenomic-contig-colinearity-analysis
description: Use when a post-assembly contig set (e.g., MergedContigs.fasta from MeGAMerge) contains very large contigs (hundreds of kb) whose contiguity must be confirmed by whole-contig colinear alignment to a single reference genome, such as Supplementary Figures S4-S5 validation.

name: metagenomic-contig-depth-estimation
description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs plus per-sample short-read FASTQs and need per-contig mean sequencing depths across samples to feed co-abundance-based binning (e.g., MetaBAT2) or to estimate MAG abundances.

name: metagenomic-contig-dereplication
description: Use when multiple assembled metagenome contig FASTA files (e.g. from SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, Velvet, Newbler) must be pooled and deduplicated prior to OLC-based merging, and exact duplicates, reverse complements, or subsequences must be eliminated first.

name: metagenomic-contig-extension
description: Use when metaSPAdes or another de novo assembler has produced viral metagenomic seed contigs of only a few kb and the goal is to lengthen them with paired or unpaired FASTQ reads while checking accuracy against NCBI viral reference sequences.

name: metagenomic-contig-set-merging
description: Use when you have multiple FASTA files of assembled contigs from different assemblers (e.g., Velvet, SOAPdenovo, IDBA, Ray, CLC Bio) or related metagenome samples and want a single improved, more contiguous merged contig set.

name: metagenomic-contig-taxonomy-annotation
description: Use when you need to classify assembled metagenomic contigs as putative viral sequences and need a reproducible confidence label based on agreement across multiple detection tools rather than a single-tool call.

name: metagenomic-count-filtering
description: Use when a mapped gene frequency count table from a mapping-based metagenomic pipeline is sparse and compositional and must be filtered, length-corrected and CSS-normalized before taxonomic or functional (KO/EC/reaction) profiling.

name: metagenomic-count-normalization
description: Use when the input is a sparse, high-throughput marker-gene (OTU/species/taxon) count matrix with two or more sample groups, and per-feature differential abundance statistics must account for both normalization and under-sampling of microbial communities.

name: metagenomic-database-construction
description: Use when constructing a k-mer/minhash classification database from large multi-kingdom reference genome collections where full-database build exceeds workstation memory, or when benchmarking build time and peak RAM across partition/executor counts.

name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when metagenomic Illumina (or 454) reads are available, multiple de novo assemblies (e.g. different kmer values or assemblers) have been generated, and improved contiguity (larger contigs, more genes) is needed beyond any single assembler run.

name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when raw or preprocessed paired-end metagenome FASTQ reads must be assembled into contigs de novo as the first step toward building or reproducing a gene catalog such as VIRGO, and assembly statistics are the deliverable.

name: metagenomic-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing metagenomic abundance profiles (taxon/gene/KO/EC/reaction tables) across phenotype groups (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma) to find significantly changed biomarker features while correcting compositional bias.

name: metagenomic-distance-behavior-validation
description: Use when you need to reproduce, reimplement, or validate scalable all-vs-all metagenome distance computation from k-mer frequency vectors, or sanity-check that a distance implementation yields near-zero self-distance.

name: metagenomic-fastq-accession-handling
description: Use when reproducing a k-mer abundance indexing/AMQ benchmark that requires concrete public metagenomic FASTQ runs — one dataset to build the index and an independent query dataset for FPR measurement.

name: metagenomic-fecal-source-tracking
description: Use when gzipped FASTQ shotgun metagenomes from water samples must be attributed to specific fecal source categories and apportioned by cell fraction, without sequencing the potential sources themselves.

name: metagenomic-flanking-region-extraction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield the genomic context (flanking regions) around ARGs or other target genes, and full de novo assembly would be computationally prohibitive.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ from fecal samples) and need functional pathway enrichment comparisons between groups rather than only taxonomic composition.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-level-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between gene-level and functional-level (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis of mapped metagenomic count data, when you have per-level significance ratios from a case-control dataset such as CAMAMED's colorectal adenoma/carcinoma (CAMAMED) run.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when installing MetaLAFFA or customizing its pipeline operation — choosing steps, per-step parameters, cluster submission settings, or reference databases (UniRef90, KEGG mappings, host decoys) — prior to annotating shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data.

name: metagenomic-functional-pathway-profiling
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic case-control data (e.g. SCZ n=344, T2D n=171) require pathway-level enrichment testing and integration with host GWAS summary statistics to evaluate pathway overlap.

name: metagenomic-functional-profiling
description: Use when metagenomic reads have already been mapped to a non-redundant gene catalog yielding per-sample gene frequencies, and the goal is to extend these into KO, EC number and reaction annotations with per-sample functional frequencies.

name: metagenomic-gene-catalogue-processing
description: Use when a metagenomic analysis needs gene clusters grouped by genomic adjacency (synteny) to associate functional content and shared pathways with MAG clusters or subspecies clades.

name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-functional-summarization
description: Use when you have MAGinator synteny_clusters.tab output plus a non-redundant gene catalogue and need to attach KEGG module assignments per synteny cluster and measure functional coherence.

name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-mining
description: Use when starting from microbial genome assemblies and needing predicted MGCs/BGCs reduced to representative GCFs as mapping targets for metagenomic or metatranscriptomic abundance analysis.

name: metagenomic-gene-count-matrix-curation
description: Use when profiling de novo MAG clusters from shotgun metagenomics requires cluster-specific signature genes: you have a gene read-count matrix (small_gene_count_matrix.tsv) and MAG cluster assignments (metagenomicspecies.tab) and need abundance-grade gene sets.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when comparing merged (MeGAMerge) vs individual metagenomic assemblies by predicted gene counts and coding density, or when annotating contigs >=2 kb without a reference genome.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads or scaftigs (FASTA) lack gene annotations and gene coordinates are required as input for operon/proximon prediction (e.g. MetaRon 'ago' or 'op' mode).

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when input is unassembled metagenomic DNA reads (e.g. Sanger, 454, or Illumina shotgun reads) and the goal is nucleotide-level gene prediction with sensitivity/precision scoring against known gene coordinates.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when you have assembled genome FASTA files (MAGs, fungal genomes, viral genomes/vOTUs) and need translated protein-coding gene sequences as input for downstream gene clustering, annotation or gene catalogue construction.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when input is a metagenome assembly FASTA (human microbiome contigs) needing gene prediction in GTF format, and near-complete-genome accuracy is required for short contigs without genomic context.

name: metagenomic-gene-to-ortholog-mapping
description: Use when you have a gene-level (e.g. UniRef90-based, length-normalized) abundance table and a gene-to-KO mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile per sample.

name: metagenomic-genome-assembly
description: Use when processing shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler and you need per-sample assembled contigs plus a single species-level non-redundant contig library (nrclib.fasta) for downstream annotation, taxonomy assignment, and analysis.

name: metagenomic-genome-dereplication
description: Use when a genome set assembled/binned from metagenomes will be used as a concatenated mapping reference or for cross-tool strain-sharing benchmarks, and redundant near-identical genomes (e.g. >98% ANI) must be collapsed first.

name: metagenomic-genome-size-estimation
description: Use when metagenomic read-mapping results (per-genome sequence depth X from CoverM against source-associated genome databases) must be normalized to genome equivalents to express source signal as approximate cell fractions.

name: metagenomic-hic-binning-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing viral binning tools on metagenomic Hi-C datasets (shotgun + Hi-C FASTQ pairs from SRA/ENA) and evaluating recovered vMAGs by completeness categories.

name: metagenomic-hic-multi-dataset-quality-benchmarking
description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads from several metagenomic Hi-C datasets and need a reference-free, quantitative measure of ligation/library quality comparable across datasets.

name: metagenomic-hit-summarization
description: Use when you have filtered read-to-gene DIAMOND alignment hits ( e-value per read) from shotgun metagenomic data and need to compute per-gene abundance counts, including fractional assignment of multi-mapping reads.

name: metagenomic-is-candidate-screening
description: Use when paired-end short-read metagenomic reads have already been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (LCoord/RCoord annotated FASTA) and sample assemblies exist, and you need proximity-filtered candidate ITR reads.

name: metagenomic-krona-chart
description: Analyze data with `metagenomic-krona-chart` using a reproducible workflow, explicit validation, and structured outputs for review-ready interpretation.

name: metagenomic-marker-consensus-sequencing
description: Use when MetaPhlAn 4 profiles detect a target species (including taxonomically unidentified SGBs) across many shotgun metagenomes and you need a strain phylogeny or strain-sharing/transmission analysis from marker alignments.

name: metagenomic-marker-database-construction
description: Use when building or reproducing a reference marker-gene database from a large genome catalog (isolates plus MAGs), e.g. deriving SGBs and unique markers underlying MetaPhlAn 4-style taxonomic profiling.

name: metagenomic-metadata-regression-modeling
description: Use when you have a microbial feature abundance table (taxonomic or functional profiles) plus sample metadata (e.g. geography, health status, extraction method) and need significant feature–variable associations from multivariable linear models.

name: metagenomic-mock-data-simulation
description: Use when a reproducible mock compositional abundance table (with matched control/disease phenotype data) is needed to test or benchmark metagenomic feature-enrichment or causality-inference methods such as VTwins.

name: metagenomic-multi-sample-contig-binning
description: Use when you have metagenomic short-read samples from multiple environments and want to bin contigs across samples jointly (multi-sample mode), comparing or replacing single-sample binners like VAMB.

name: metagenomic-pipeline-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify wall-clock time, peak memory footprint, and CPU-hour usage of a Snakemake-based metagenomic pipeline (e.g. ARGprofiler with fastp, KMA, ARGextender, SPAdes, Mash rules) under its final parameter settings.

name: metagenomic-preprocessing
description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be cleaned before functional annotation — removing human/host reads, PCR or optical duplicates, and low-quality or too-short reads prior to gene mapping.

name: metagenomic-preprocessing-pipeline
description: Use when raw metagenomic samples arrive as SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA, quality-checked, and characterized with per-sample sequence statistics before taxonomic/functional mapping.

name: metagenomic-profiler-versus-ground-truth-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic profiler against a known ground truth (e.g. CAMI marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and you need clade-level presence/absence discordance beyond F1 or UniFrac scores.

name: metagenomic-protein-assembly
description: Use when the goal is to maximize protein sequence recovery from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic short-read data (paired-end FASTQ or single-end FASTA/FASTQ) by assembling directly at the protein level.

name: metagenomic-protein-database-construction
description: Use when analyzing metaproteomics tandem MS/MS spectra against metagenome-derived protein databases (metapeptide or non-redundant environmental FASTA), or when benchmarking database search vs de novo peptide-detection counts.

name: metagenomic-protein-sequence-screening
description: Use when you need to identify and type-classify proteins (e.g. DsrA/DsrB and paralogous families) in thousands of (meta)genomic protein sequences in FASTA format, at scale, without phylogenetic reconstruction.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., the 30-sample BIO-ML set from PRJNA544527 or a 121-sample H. pylori eradication cohort) must be mapped to a reference database to generate per-sample BAMs for downstream variant detection.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment
description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be mapped to a combined microbiome reference FASTA while preserving junction pairs mapping across different references, as the first stage of LEMON's HGT detection pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-gene-catalog
description: Use when you have QC'd shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads and a non-redundant gene catalog (e.g., the IGC catalog), and you need per-sample gene frequencies as input to compositional differential-abundance analysis.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-genome-databases
description: Use when assigning shotgun metagenomic reads from water or mesocosm samples (e.g. FASTQ reads from PRJNA1161616) to individual genomes in a source-associated database to quantify per-genome and per-source-category signal.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-operons
description: Use when you have predicted operon sequences from metagenomic shotgun samples and raw paired-end reads, and need per-sample pathway/KO abundances to compare disease versus control groups.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-viral-scaffolds
description: Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) must be binned from metagenomes and per-sample coverage tables are needed as input to vRhyme's coverage variance / effect-size binning network.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina FASTQ, single- or paired-end) from metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to NCBI taxa, especially when reference genomes are incomplete or distant strains must still be classified.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying shotgun FASTQ/FASTA reads from complex biological samples (e.g., calibrator sausage mixtures) against large reference genome collections to detect ingredient/species composition and estimate abundances with low false-positive rates.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. simulated setA2/setB2 or HMP metagenome SRR1804065) against a reference genome FASTA in alignment-free fashion, computing sensitivity/precision/F1/specificity.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying fastq/fasta metagenomic reads at species or genus rank, especially gut microbiome reads from uncultured MAGs where k-mer/LCA tools miss species absent from reference databases.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when assigning taxonomic labels to large sets of metagenomic reads (FASTQ/FASTA from SRA accessions such as SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055, or Mason-simulated reads), or when benchmarking classifier speed and accuracy against Megablast or MetaPhlAn.

name: metagenomic-read-classification-kraken2
description: Reference for applying Kraken 2 to classify 16S amplicon reads from mock community samples at species/genus level and comparing its accuracy against 16S-specific pipelines over matched reference libraries.

name: metagenomic-read-clustering
description: Use when metagenomic Illumina short reads must be split into strain/species-coherent read groups before per-cluster assembly, e.g. as the preprocessing step of an overlap-layout-consensus strain-aware assembly pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-coordinate-processing
description: Use when scanning metagenomic FASTA reads with pal-MEM for inverted terminal repeats and you need to encode read coordinates in two-bit space, apply edge-boundary conditions, or exclude MEMs near read ends that arise from amplification artifacts.

name: metagenomic-read-counting-per-taxon
description: Use when you already have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query run and need organism-level read counts and abundance percentages at a chosen rank such as species.

name: metagenomic-read-decontamination
description: Use when untargeted Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical or animal samples contain host (e.g. human, mouse, mastomys), reagent, or bacterial contamination that must be removed before viral de novo assembly.

name: metagenomic-read-digital-normalization
description: Use when raw paired-end virome FASTQ reads (e.g. SRA runs like SRR3458562 or SRR9875293) feed into VirMAP's mapping assembly, pileup rebuilding, or DIAMOND/BBMap alignment and read depth is uneven or redundant.

name: metagenomic-read-gene-annotation
description: Use when per-sample DIAMOND tabular hits against a gene catalog (e.g. UniRef90) need -e-value refinement and fractional gene counting to produce gene/orthology abundances from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs.

name: metagenomic-read-length-and-n-trimming
description: Use when raw or primer-trimmed amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina) show deteriorating 3'-end quality or embedded Ns and must be trimmed and length-filtered before dereplication and OTU clustering.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping
description: Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads need to be mapped to a multi-genome reference .fasta to quantify genome detection, coverage, microdiversity, or strain sharing (e.g., ZymoBIOMICS mock-community benchmarking).

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-abundance-profiling
description: Use when you have predicted MGC/BGC regions from antiSMASH/gutSMASH genomes plus shotgun metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads (e.g., SRA accessions) and need RPKM abundance profiles and phenotype-differential cluster statistics.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-and-counting
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be quantified against de novo MAG clusters or signature gene sets to estimate organism/subspecies abundances per sample, e.g. tracking B. infantis and B. longum across the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-quantification
description: Use when short-read shotgun metagenomes (FASTQ) must be converted from mapped-read counts into genome-equivalent relative abundances (cell fractions) against a source-associated genome database for source tracking.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-contigs
description: Use when you need to judge assembly quality by read support: you have assembled contig FASTA files (individual or merged) and matching trimmed reads, and want per-contig base-coverage percentages.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-gene-catalog
description: Use when you need to profile the taxonomic and/or functional composition of vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ samples against the VIRGO gene catalog instead of assembling reads de novo.

name: metagenomic-read-pair-filtering
description: Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (e.g. concatenated .fasta) and per-scaffold or per-genome coverage, clonality, nucleotide diversity, or SNV calls must be computed without contamination from falsely mapped read pairs.

name: metagenomic-read-pooling-and-spike-in-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a targeted assembly or annotation pipeline (e.g. CasCollect) against a complete metagenome assembly, and a simulated community with known CRISPR/Cas content and background host contamination is needed from raw FASTQ reads.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw metagenomic sequencing FASTQ files must be converted into clean, host-free reads before taxonomic or functional profiling, or when reproducing the Liu 2020 metagenomic pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed before SSU rRNA read extraction or any 16S/18S-based taxonomic classification.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic fastq reads must be cleaned (human/rRNA removal) and mapped to a reference gene catalog such as VIRGO before taxonomic or functional profiling.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when quality-controlling shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as part of an end-to-end functional annotation pipeline, after host and duplicate read filtering and before mapping reads to a gene database.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA accession SRR606249, 2 x 100 bp) must be cleaned prior to meta-assembly with metaSPAdes or MegaHIT.

name: metagenomic-read-query-execution
description: Use when benchmarking fimpera-style amplified s-mer querying of a counting Bloom filter on metagenomic FASTQ reads, specifically to verify that query time stays flat or slightly decreases as z increases.

name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-analysis
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a reference gene catalogue's sequence-capture efficiency on shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples, or comparing a new catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) against an incumbent (e.g. VIRGO) via per-sample mapping rates.

name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-targeted-assembly
description: Use when you need genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (or other target genes) from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data, and full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic abundance profiler (e.g. BiG-MAP) against known truth: you need simulated shotgun libraries with known gene-cluster abundances to sweep parameter grids (MASH cutoff × Bowtie2 mode) and compute F1.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier needs simulated reads with known origin, e.g., ART-generated Illumina/Roche-454 FASTQ sets from genomes whose proteins are excluded from the reference database.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain SNVs and small InDels with configurable allele-frequency trajectories, to benchmark mutation-detection tools.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction pipelines against known ground truth, so sensitivity and FDR can be computed from simulated reads at defined coverages.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation-and-alignment
description: Use when benchmarking metagenome binners against curated ground-truth genomes: simulated/sampled per-sample reads must be converted into sorted BAM coverage files and ORF predictions before binning and F1/precision/specificity scoring.

name: metagenomic-read-subsampling
description: Use when a genome in a simulated community is assembled at extreme coverage (e.g. >1000x) and you need to confirm that coverage — not biology — drives the observed misassembled blocks.

name: metagenomic-read-subsampling-replication
description: Use when a user wants to quantify how classification sensitivity and reconstruction completeness degrade with sequencing depth, e.g. testing a pipeline on SRA mock-community reads (FASTQ) at 10/1/0.1% subsampling across replicate trials.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-attribution
description: Use when disease-associated genes from MWAS must be assigned to taxa in a shotgun metagenome, e.g., tracing which organisms reads of a specific gene derive from.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when you have FASTQ read fractions (mapped/unmapped from read-contig alignment) from a HiFi metagenome assembly and need to know whether low-representation taxa are missing from the assembly.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when quality-assuring preprocessed short-read FASTQ metagenomic samples prior to assembly: to classify reads against a reference database, detect contamination, and visualize microbial community composition per sample with Krona charts and a MultiQC report.

name: metagenomic-read-to-protein-alignment
description: Use when quality-filtered (host-filtered, duplicate-filtered, quality-trimmed) shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be mapped to a microbial protein gene database like UniRef90 to obtain read-to-gene matches for functional profiling.

name: metagenomic-read-type-gating
description: Use when a metagenomic run mixes short-read-only, long-read-only, and paired short+long-read samples, and each sample must be routed to the correct assembly path (MEGAHIT vs SPAdes vs hybridSPAdes) before QUAST-based quality comparison.

name: metagenomic-reference-catalog-retrieval
description: Use when a study needs large, publicly available, redundancy-filtered reference protein catalogs (e.g. as search database input for HH-suite3/BFD or for catalog size/provenance audits) and the input is metagenomic or metatranscriptomic protein sequence space.

name: metagenomic-reference-sequence-comparison
description: Use when candidate transferred segments reconstructed from shotgun metagenomics data must be scored against donor/receptor reference segment sequences to measure local alignment similarity and reconstruction accuracy.

name: metagenomic-sample-metadata-stratification
description: Use when a Qiita-deposited fecal shotgun metagenomics feature table (n=666 paired SPF fecal samples) with metadata fields genotype/study/sex/cohort must be subset (e.g., Sacrifice cohort, per-study) before PERMANOVA or beta-diversity testing.

name: metagenomic-sample-phenotype-classification
description: Use when you have a metagenomic taxonomic profile table (MetaPhlAn merged table or QIIME OTU/BIOM) plus sample metadata with class labels, and the goal is to train a classifier or predict the phenotype of unknown samples.

name: metagenomic-scaffold-sequence-processing

name: microbiome-feature-table-analysis

name: mitug-01-business
description: שלב א׳ במיתוג — הכרת העסק ובעל העסק לעומק: מה העסק מוכר בפועל, מי עומד מאחוריו, מה החזון, לאן הוא רוצה להגיע, ומה נקודות החוזק והתורפה. הפעל כשמתחילים תהליך מיתוג, וגם על: "בוא נכיר את העסק", "מה החזון שלי", "לאן אני רוצה להגיע עם העסק", "מה המטרות של העסק", "ספר לי על העסק שלך", business discovery, brand foundation. זהו השלב הראשון — כל שאר השלבים נשענים עליו.

name: mitug-02-audience
description: שלב ב׳ במיתוג — הכרת פלח השוק וזיהוי קהל היעד: למי בדיוק העסק פונה, איפה הקהל נמצא, מה יניע אותו לפעולה, ובמה להתמקד. הפעל על: "מי קהל היעד שלי", "למי אני מוכר", "פלח שוק", "הקהל שלי זה כולם", "איך אני יודע במה להתמקד", "אני לא יודע למי לפנות", target audience, market segment, customer persona, ICP. השלב שמונע את הכשל הנפוץ ביותר — מיתוג שמדבר לכולם ולכן לא מדבר לאף אחד.

name: mitug-03-concept
description: שלב ג׳ במיתוג — גיבוש הקונספט, השלב החשוב ביותר בתהליך: מחקר תחום ומתחרים, זיקוק ערכי מותג, וניסוח מסר המותג כערך ללקוח. הפעל על: "מה הקונספט של העסק", "ערכי מותג", "מחקר מתחרים", "מה המסר שלי", "במה אני שונה מהמתחרים", "בידול", "מה הרעיון שמוביל את המותג", brand concept, brand values, positioning, competitive research, brand message. הקונספט הוא האסטרטגיה שמובילה את כל העיצוב והמסרים — בלעדיו השם והלוגו הם ניחוש.

name: mitug-04-name
description: שלב ד׳ במיתוג — בחירת שם לעסק: שמונת כיווני השם עם היתרונות והחסרונות של כל אחד, רשימת ההימנעות המלאה, ובדיקות תקינות (בין־לאומית, דומיין, קריאוּת). הפעל על: "איזה שם לתת לעסק", "צריך שם", "השם שלי לא עובד", "לשנות שם לעסק", "תציע לי שמות", "בדוק לי את השם", business name, naming, brand name, rename. חובה לבחור שם לפני שמעצבים לוגו — לא להפך.

description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 事故应急。当用户请求应急处理生产事故，或调用 moma-incident 指令时使用本技能， 按"先止血、后定位、再修复防复发"三步处理生产事故：优先回滚或降级等可逆止血措施，再定位根因， 写入事故记录并将正式修复交 /moma-fix。紧急情况可先止血后补登记，但事后必须补齐。

name: moma-init
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 项目启动。当用户请求启动新项目并生成文档，或调用 moma-init 指令时使用本技能， 从用户的自然语言需求出发，按阶段1（需求定义）→ 阶段2（技术设计）→ 阶段3（开发约束）的顺序 生成全套项目文档（01~07），为后续 /moma-coding 编码做准备。本指令仅生成文档，不进入编码阶段。

name: moma-migrate
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 数据库迁移。当用户请求执行数据模型迁移，或调用 moma-migrate 指令时使用本技能， 执行数据模型变更的高危流程：先同步更新 04-数据模型文档，再生成可回滚的迁移脚本与回滚方案， 确认备份并获用户逐项授权后执行，执行后验证数据。物理删除数据必须获用户明确确认。

name: moma-modify
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 需求调整。当用户请求调整已有需求，或调用 moma-modify 指令时使用本技能， 调整已有需求（含功能删减）并同步更新 01/02 文档及受影响的下游文档，随后按需进行代码变更， 在 changes/ 目录下新建变更记录文件，并以 modify: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。

name: moma-new
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 功能新增。当用户请求新增一个功能，或调用 moma-new 指令时使用本技能， 增加原有需求中未描述的全新功能，定位归属模块后同步更新 01/02 及受影响的下游文档， 按需进行代码变更，在 changes/ 目录下新建变更记录文件，并以 feat: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。

name: moma-optimize
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 功能优化。当用户请求细化或优化已有功能，或调用 moma-optimize 指令时使用本技能， 对已有需求进行更详细的约束和优化（细化现有功能的行为边界，而非新增功能），同步更新 01/02 及受影响的下游文档， 按需进行代码变更，在 changes/ 目录下新建变更记录文件，并以 optimize: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。 也支持纯重构模式：外部行为不变时跳过文档更新。

name: moma-release

name: moma-retro

name: moma-review

name: moma-security

name: moma-session-complete

name: moma-soft-dev

name: moma-sync

description: 创建或审查Architecture Decision Record，记录已经作出的、影响系统结构/质量属性且难以逆转的决策、上下文、替代方案和后果。用于RFC接受后、重大技术选型、迁移或替代既有架构决定。

name: moonweave-code-review
description: PRやdiffに対して証拠駆動のレビューを行い、正当性、設計、複雑さ、テスト、契約、セキュリティ、プライバシー、AI/Agent、具身、パフォーマンス、観測性、デプロイ、ドキュメントを網羅し、重大度別に実行可能な指摘を示す。GitHub PR Review、マージ前チェック、独立監査に使用する。

name: moonweave-code-review
description: 对PR或diff进行证据驱动的审查，覆盖正确性、设计、复杂性、测试、契约、安全、隐私、AI/Agent、具身、性能、可观测、部署和文档；按严重度给出可操作意见。用于GitHub PR Review、pre-merge检查或独立审计。

name: moonweave-code-review
description: Perform evidence-driven review of PRs or diffs, covering correctness, design, complexity, testing, contracts, security, privacy, AI/Agent, embodiment, performance, observability, deployment, and documentation; produce actionable findings by severity. Use for GitHub PR Review, pre-merge checks, or independent audit.

name: moonweave-community-contribution
description: 处理外部贡献、首次Issue/PR、非代码贡献、AI辅助贡献、Mentorship和社区冲突，保证入口清晰、反馈具体、贡献可认可、维护者负担受控且行为准则可执行。

name: moonweave-community-contribution
description: 外部貢献、初回Issue/PR、非コード貢献、AI支援貢献、Mentorship、コミュニティ紛争を処理し、参入ポイントを明確に、フィードバックを具体的に、貢献を認知可能に、メンテナ負荷を管理下に、行動規範を執行可能に保つ。

name: moonweave-community-contribution
description: Handle external contributions, first Issues/PRs, non-code contributions, AI-assisted contributions, Mentorship, and community conflict; keep entry points clear, feedback specific, contributions recognizable, maintainer load controlled, and the Code of Conduct enforceable.

name: moonweave-documentation
description: Create, refactor, or review knowledge assets such as README, Tutorial, How-to, Reference, Explanation, API docs, Runbook, and Model/Dataset/Agent Cards, ensuring a single source of truth, Owner, status, metadata, links, review, and lifecycle.

name: moonweave-documentation
description: README、Tutorial、How-to、Reference、Explanation、APIドキュメント、Runbook、Model/Dataset/Agent Cardなどのナレッジ資産を作成・リファクタ・レビューし、単一の事実源、Owner、ステータス、メタデータ、リンク、Review、ライフサイクルを確保する。

name: moonweave-documentation
description: 创建、重构或审查README、Tutorial、How-to、Reference、Explanation、API文档、Runbook、Model/Dataset/Agent Card等知识资产，确保单一事实源、Owner、状态、元数据、链接、Review和生命周期。

name: moonweave-engineering-brief
description: Write an Engineering Brief for standard or high-risk engineering changes, defining domain concepts, state, invariants, interfaces, and failure modes first, then implementation, technology selection, testing, observability, deployment, and rollback. Use before formal development begins or when a PR is too large and needs upfront design.

name: moonweave-engineering-brief
description: 標準または高リスクのエンジニアリング変更に対するEngineering Briefを作成し、ドメイン概念、状態、不変条件、インターフェース、失敗モードを先に定義し、その後実装、技術選定、テスト、観測、デプロイ、ロールバックを決定する。正式開発前やPRが大きく事前設計が必要な場合に使用。

name: moonweave-engineering-brief
description: 为标准或高风险工程变更撰写Engineering Brief，先定义领域概念、状态、不变量、接口和失败模式，再确定实现、技术选型、测试、观测、部署和回滚。用于进入正式开发前或PR过大需要前置设计时。

name: moonweave-flow
description: Run a staged multi-skill flow for the current project phase. First audit the project to determine its phase (idea, engineering, major-refactor/RFC, release, operation, or retirement), list the upcoming staged steps, and ask the user to confirm the phase and consent before executing the full staged flow. Each stage invokes the appropriate Moonweave skill and gates; high-risk stages still require their own reviews and human confirmation.

name: moonweave-flow
description: 現在のプロジェクトフェーズに対し段階的なマルチskillフローを実行する。まずプロジェクトを監査してフェーズ(idea、engineering、major-refactor/RFC、release、operation、retirement)を決定し、今後の段階的ステップを列挙し、全段階的フローを実行する前にユーザーにフェーズの確認と同意を求める。各stageは適切なMoonweave skillとゲートを呼び出し、高リスクのstageには独自のレビューと人間の確認が依然必要。

name: moonweave-flow
description: 为当前项目阶段运行分阶段的多 skill 流程。先审计项目以确定其阶段(idea、engineering、major-refactor/RFC、release、operation 或 retirement),列出即将进行的分阶段步骤,并在执行完整分阶段流程前请求用户确认阶段并同意。每个阶段调用相应的 Moonweave skill 与门禁;高风险阶段仍需各自审查与人类确认。

name: moonweave-gap-analysis
description: Compare the project's current facts against Moonweave governance requirements, identify missing Owners, decisions, tests, docs, risk reviews, automation, handoffs, and runtime evidence, and convert repeated manual corrections into rules, skills, CI, or templates. Use for gap filling, quarterly reviews, and governance drift treatment.

name: moonweave-gap-analysis
description: 比较项目当前事实与Moonweave治理要求，识别缺失Owner、决策、测试、文档、风险审查、自动化、交接和运行证据，并把重复人工纠正转化为规则、技能、CI或模板。用于补漏、季度Review和治理漂移治理。

name: moonweave-gap-analysis
description: プロジェクトの現在の事実をMoonweaveガバナンス要件と比較し、欠落しているOwner、意思決定、テスト、ドキュメント、リスクレビュー、自動化、引き継ぎ、実行時エビデンスを特定し、繰り返される手動修正をルール、スキル、CI、テンプレートに変換する。補漏、四半期Review、ガバナンスドリフト治理に使用する。

name: moonweave-governance-change
description: Moonweaveの原則、Governance、コラボレーション、エンジニアリング、品質、知識、またはskills自体を変更する際、Governance RFC、影響分析、後方互換性、プラットフォーム適合、評価、バージョニング、移行を実行する。Governanceリポジトリの更新、skillの追加/変更、プラットフォームアダプタの適合に使用する。

name: moonweave-governance-change
description: 修改辉夜计划原则、治理、协作、工程、质量、知识或skills本身时，执行治理RFC、影响分析、向后兼容、平台适配、评测、版本和迁移流程。用于更新governance仓库、增加/修改skill或平台适配器。

name: moonweave-governance-change
description: When modifying Moonweave principles, governance, collaboration, engineering, quality, knowledge, or the skills themselves, execute a governance RFC, impact analysis, backward compatibility, platform adaptation, evaluation, versioning, and migration. Used to update the governance repository, add/modify a skill, or adapt platform adapters.

name: moonweave-governance-router
description: 对任何项目请求、Issue、PR、设计或事故先做治理分类：识别工作类型、S0-S5风险、QA-L0-L5质量等级、M0-M9成熟度、所需Owner/DRI、RFC/ADR/安全/评测/具身门禁，并把任务路由到正确的Moonweave技能。用于不确定下一步、开始复杂工作或需要治理总览时。

name: moonweave-governance-router
description: Apply governance triage to any project request, Issue, PR, design, or incident first — identify work type, S0-S5 risk, QA-L0-L5 quality level, M0-M9 maturity, required Owner/DRI, and RFC/ADR/security/eval/embodiment gates, then route the task to the correct Moonweave skill. Use when unsure of the next step, starting complex work, or needing a governance overview.

name: moonweave-governance-router
description: あらゆるプロジェクト依頼、Issue、PR、設計、インシデントに対してまずガバナンスのトリアージを行う。作業タイプ、S0-S5リスク、QA-L0-L5品質レベル、M0-M9成熟度、必要なOwner/DRI、RFC/ADR/セキュリティ/評価/具現化ゲートを識別し、タスクを適切なMoonweaveスキルにルーティングする。次のステップが不明な場合、複雑な作業を開始する場合、ガバナンスの全体像が必要な場合に使用する。

name: moonweave-handoff
description: DRI/Ownerの一時離脱、役割変更、プロジェクト一時停止、インシデント交代、ワーキンググループ終了、リポジトリ移行のための実行可能なHandoffを作成し、Owner Registry、アクセスパス、リスク、次のステップ、受領確認を更新する。

name: moonweave-handoff
description: Create an actionable Handoff for DRI/Owner temporary absence, role changes, project pauses, incident shift changes, working group closeout, or repository transfer; update the Owner Registry, access paths, risks, next steps, and receipt confirmation.

name: moonweave-handoff
description: 为DRI/Owner暂离、角色变化、项目暂停、事故换班、工作组结束或仓库移交创建可执行Handoff，更新Owner Registry、访问路径、风险、下一步和接收确认。

name: moonweave-help
description: Help a user pick the right Moonweave skill or command for their current situation. Describe the 25 skills grouped by phase, ask one clarifying question when intent is ambiguous, and recommend the best next skill with a one-line reason. Use when the user asks "which skill should I use", "what command do I run", or is otherwise unsure how to start.

name: moonweave-help
description: 帮用户为当前情境选择合适的 Moonweave skill 或命令。按阶段分组介绍 25 个 skill,在意图不明确时提出一个澄清问题,并用一句话理由推荐最佳下一步 skill。当用户问"该用哪个 skill""该跑什么命令"或不确定如何起步时使用。

name: moonweave-help
description: ユーザーの現状に合った Moonweave skill またはコマンドの選択を支援する。25個のskillをフェーズ別にグループ化して提示し、意図が曖昧な場合は1つの明確化質問を行い、1行の理由とともに最適な次のskillを推奨する。ユーザーが「どのskillを使うべきか」「どのコマンドを実行するか」と尋ねる場合や、どう始めるか迷っている場合に使用。

name: moonweave-idea-triage
description: Turn scattered ideas, feedback, incident improvements, or research questions into actionable Idea/Discovery records — complete type, Area, risk, Owner, priority, evidence, and next-step routing. Use for new ideas, requirement clarification, backlog cleanup, and judging whether a project is worth doing.

name: moonweave-idea-triage
description: 散在なアイデア、フィードバック、インシデント改善、研究問いを実行可能なIdea/Discoveryレコードに変換する。タイプ、Area、リスク、Owner、優先度、エビデンス、次のステップのルーティングを完了する。新規アイデア、要件の明確化、バックログ整理、プロジェクト価値の判断に使用する。

name: moonweave-idea-triage
description: 把零散想法、反馈、事故改进或研究问题转成可判断的Idea/Discovery记录，完成类型、Area、风险、Owner、优先级、证据和下一步分流。用于新想法、需求澄清、backlog清理和项目是否值得做的判断。

name: moonweave-implementation
description: 既にEngineering Readyのコードまたはシステム変更を実行し、短命ブランチ、小さなコミット、再現可能な環境、ローカル検証、スコープ制御、依存ガバナンス、テスト/ドキュメント同期に従う。実際の開発、リファクタリング、修正、クロスファイル実装に使用。

name: moonweave-implementation
description: Execute code or system changes that are already Engineering Ready, following short branches, small commits, reproducible environments, local verification, scope control, dependency governance, and test/doc synchronization. Use for actual development, refactoring, fixes, and cross-file implementation.

name: moonweave-implementation
description: 执行已经Engineering Ready的代码或系统变更，遵循短分支、小步提交、可复现环境、本地验证、范围控制、依赖治理、测试与文档同步。用于实际开发、重构、修复和跨文件实现。

name: moonweave-incident-response
description: 本番障害、セキュリティ脆弱性、データ破損、Agentの権限越境、Embodied異常、重大なリグレッションを処理する：単一タイムライン、Incident DRI、影響コミュニケーション、緩和/ロールバック、証拠保全、非公開開示、非難責ポストモーテムを確立する。

name: moonweave-incident-response
description: 处理生产中断、安全漏洞、数据损坏、Agent越权、具身异常或重大回归：建立单一时间线、Incident DRI、影响沟通、缓解/回滚、证据保全、私密披露和无责复盘。

name: moonweave-incident-response
description: Handle production outages, security vulnerabilities, data corruption, Agent overreach, embodied anomalies, or major regressions by establishing a single timeline, an Incident DRI, impact communication, mitigation/rollback, evidence preservation, private disclosure, and a blameless postmortem.

name: moonweave-issue
description: 创建或改进可执行的GitHub Issue，覆盖Bug、Feature、Research、Experiment、Security、Docs、Migration与Release任务；确保上下文、范围、验收、Owner、风险和关联决策完整。

name: moonweave-issue
description: Create or refine actionable GitHub Issues covering Bug, Feature, Research, Experiment, Security, Docs, Migration, and Release tasks; ensure context, scope, acceptance, Owner, risk, and linked decisions are complete.

name: moonweave-issue
description: Bug、Feature、Research、Experiment、Security、Docs、Migration、Releaseタスクを含む実行可能なGitHub Issueを作成または改善し、コンテキスト、スコープ、验收、Owner、リスク、関連決定が完全であることを確保する。

name: moonweave-project-bootstrap
description: 为新的辉夜计划仓库、服务、库、数据/模型项目或具身子项目建立Engineering Ready基线、Owner、风险与质量声明、标准文件、CI骨架、Agent配置和首次审计。用于创建项目、接管遗留仓库或把原型提升为正式工程。

name: moonweave-project-bootstrap
description: 新しいMoonweaveリポジトリ、サービス、ライブラリ、データ/モデルプロジェクト、具現化サブプロジェクトにEngineering Readyベースラインを構築する。Owner、リスク・品質宣言、標準ファイル、CIスケルトン、Agent設定、初回監査を行う。プロジェクト作成、レガシーリポジトリの引き継ぎ、プロトタイプの正式エンジニアリングへの引き上げ時に使用する。

name: moonweave-project-bootstrap
description: Establish an Engineering Ready baseline for a new Moonweave repo, service, library, data/model project, or embodiment subproject — Owner, risk and quality declarations, standard files, CI skeleton, Agent configuration, and a first audit. Use when creating a project, taking over a legacy repo, or promoting a prototype to formal engineering.

name: moonweave-project-planning
description: 検証済みの問題やプロトタイプを実行可能なプロジェクト計画に分解する。ライフサイクル状態、M0-M9成熟度、マイルストーン、Issue、依存、Owner/DRI、品質エビデンス、リリース、終了条件を定義する。プロジェクト計画、Roadmap、Milestone、プロトタイプ昇格、一時停止/アーカイブ意思決定に使用する。

name: moonweave-project-planning
description: Break a validated problem or prototype into an executable project plan — lifecycle state, M0-M9 maturity, milestones, Issues, dependencies, Owner/DRI, quality evidence, release, and exit conditions. Use for project planning, Roadmap, Milestone, prototype promotion, and pause/archive decisions.

name: moonweave-project-planning
description: 把已验证的问题或原型拆解成可执行的项目计划：生命周期状态、M0-M9成熟度、里程碑、Issue、依赖、Owner/DRI、质量证据、发布和退出条件。用于项目规划、Roadmap、Milestone、原型晋级和暂停/归档决策。

name: moonweave-pull-request
description: Package implementation into a reviewable Pull Request: control scope, link Issue/RFC/ADR, explain motivation, tests, compatibility, security, AI/Agent, deployment, and rollback, and check Ready conditions. Use to open a PR, update a PR description, or prepare for merge.

name: moonweave-pull-request
description: 実装をレビュー可能なPull Requestにまとめる。スコープを制御し、Issue/RFC/ADRをリンクし、動機、テスト、互換性、セキュリティ、AI/Agent、デプロイ、ロールバックを説明し、Ready条件を確認する。PR作成、PR説明の更新、マージ準備に使用する。

name: moonweave-pull-request
description: 把实现整理成可审查的Pull Request：控制范围、链接Issue/RFC/ADR、说明动机、测试、兼容、安全、AI/Agent、部署和回滚，并检查Ready条件。用于开PR、更新PR描述或准备合并。

name: moonweave-quality-assurance
description: ソフトウェア、サービス、データ、モデル、Agent、または具身システムに対してQA-L0-L5を決定し、テスト階層と品質エビデンスを設計し、Q0-Q5のゲートを実行し、Flaky test、品質負債、リリースブロッカーを特定する。テスト計画、CIゲート、品質レビュー、本番準備に使用する。

name: moonweave-quality-assurance
description: 为软件、服务、数据、模型、Agent或具身系统确定QA-L0-L5，设计测试分层和质量证据，执行Q0-Q5门禁，识别Flaky test、质量债和发布阻断。用于测试计划、CI门禁、质量审查和生产就绪。

name: moonweave-quality-assurance
description: Determine QA-L0-L5 for software, services, data, models, Agents, or embodied systems; design test layers and quality evidence; execute Q0-Q5 gates; identify flaky tests, quality debt, and release blockers. Use for test planning, CI gates, quality reviews, and production readiness.

name: moonweave-release-readiness
description: 执行Release Readiness、制品追溯、迁移/回滚、监控、SLO、灰度和上线后验证；输出Go/No-Go/Conditional Go。用于版本发布、生产部署、模型/Agent上线或具身能力释放。

name: moonweave-release-readiness
description: Release Readiness、アーティファクト追跡、マイグレーション/ロールバック、監視、SLO、段階的ロールアウト、ローンチ後検証を実行し、Go/No-Go/Conditional Goを出力する。バージョンリリース、本番デプロイ、モデル/Agentローンチ、具身能力リリースに使用する。

name: moonweave-release-readiness
description: Execute Release Readiness, artifact traceability, migration/rollback, monitoring, SLO, staged rollout, and post-launch verification; output Go/No-Go/Conditional Go. Use for version releases, production deployments, model/Agent launches, or embodied capability releases.

name: moonweave-repository-audit
description: Perform a read-only audit of any Moonweave project repository, checking governance installation, Owners, risk/quality claims, README/SECURITY/CODEOWNERS, CI, dependency locking, Issue/PR templates, tests, docs, AI/data/embodiment-specific evidence, and potential secrets; output a trackable remediation plan.

name: moonweave-repository-audit
description: 对任意辉夜计划仓库执行只读审计，检查治理安装、Owner、风险/质量声明、README/SECURITY/CODEOWNERS、CI、依赖锁定、Issue/PR模板、测试、文档、AI/数据/具身专项证据和潜在secret；输出可追踪补漏计划。

name: moonweave-repository-audit
description: 任意のMoonweaveプロジェクトリポジトリに対して読み取り専用監査を実行し、ガバナンスインストール、Owner、リスク/品質宣言、README/SECURITY/CODEOWNERS、CI、依存ロック、Issue/PRテンプレート、テスト、ドキュメント、AI/データ/具身特有のエビデンス、潜在的secretをチェックし、追跡可能な是正計画を出力する。

name: moonweave-research
description: 研究実験、論文Review、再現、Dataset/Model Card、Eval記録を設計・実行・レビューし、仮説、コード/データ/モデル/設定/ハードウェア/乱数シード、生結果、ネガティブ結果、制限、次のステップを追跡可能にする。

name: moonweave-research
description: 设计、执行或审查研究实验、论文Review、复现、Dataset/Model Card和Eval记录，保证假设、代码/数据/模型/配置/硬件/随机种子、原始结果、负面结果、限制和下一步可追溯。

name: moonweave-research
description: Design, execute, or review research experiments, paper reviews, reproductions, Dataset/Model Cards, and Eval records, ensuring hypotheses, code/data/model/config/hardware/random seeds, raw results, negative results, limitations, and next steps are traceable.

name: moonweave-retrospective
description: 在发布、里程碑、事故、实验、RFC或长期任务结束后进行结构化反思，比较预期与实际，识别系统性原因、治理盲区和可复用知识，并形成有Owner的改进闭环。

name: moonweave-retrospective
description: Conduct structured reflection after a release, milestone, incident, experiment, RFC, or long-running task; compare expected vs. actual, identify systemic causes, governance blind spots, and reusable knowledge, and form an Owner-bearing improvement loop.

name: moonweave-retrospective

name: msms-intensity-normalization-to-unit-sum
description: Use when a centroided MS/MS spectrum has been cleaned (peaks merged within +/- 0.05 Da, noise-filtered) and you need intensities as a probability distribution for spectral entropy or entropy-similarity calculations.

name: msms-intensity-weighting
description: Use when a centroided, normalized MS/MS peak list must be intensity-weighted prior to entropy similarity computation and the spectrum's entropy (or ion richness) is unknown or low (S < 3).

name: msms-library-count-verification

name: msms-library-matching

name: msms-longitudinal-fragment-profiling-scoring

name: msms-metadata-harmonization

name: msms-mist-fingerprint

name: msms-modified-cosine-similarity-scoring

name: msms-modified-cosine-spectral-matching
description: Use when you have paired genome–metabolome samples (PoDP-style, e.g. the 1,040-sample GNPS job task=b915d1f78c364bf4be9900047760d95c) and reference or cryptic MS/MS spectra that must be converted into similarity fingerprints for BGC–metabolite linking.

name: msms-molecular-networking

name: msms-multiple-spectral-alignment-across-molecular-family

name: msms-neutral-loss-annotation

name: msms-neutral-loss-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting ICEBERG fragment attribution outputs — e.g., after running predict_smis.py on held-out molecules — to check whether breakage frequencies and hydrogen shifts match chemistry intuition (C-O/C-N favored over C-C; -1H ↔ H2O loss).

name: msms-noise-denoising
description: Use when raw MS/MS query spectra (e.g., AD plasma from Orbitrap Astral or Exploris 240) contain electronic and chemical noise ions, and the goal is higher-confidence compound annotation via spectral library matching with entropy similarity.

name: msms-noise-filtering
description: Use when raw MS2 fragmentation spectra paired to MS1 peaks contain noisy fragment or neutral-loss entries that must be removed before building a bag-of-fragments matrix or running topic-model inference.

name: msms-noise-ion-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS library-matching similarity scores for robustness: you have cleaned, centroided reference spectra and need to quantify score degradation as artificial noise ions are added at graded levels.

name: msms-pairwise-similarity-computation

name: msms-pattern-interpretation

name: msms-peak-filtering

name: msms-peak-formula-annotation-matching
description: Use when comparing predicted formula annotations against expert-curated peak annotations on held-out MS/MS spectra (e.g., NIST20 scaffold-split test set) to score formula-level agreement of C2MS models such as FraGNNet, GrAFF-MS, or ICEBERG.

name: msms-peak-fragment-matching

name: msms-peak-intensity-coverage-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how much of the total peak intensity of real MS/MS spectra (e.g., NIST20, [M+H]+, HCD Orbitrap) is explained by an approximate fragmentation DAG with given depth d and hydrogen tolerance j.

name: msms-peak-list-extraction
description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum loaded from an MGF file must have low relative-intensity peaks removed via matchms, and you need the retained and filtered-out peak lists for inspection.

name: msms-peak-list-format-conversion
description: Use when raw MS/MS contest or experiment peak lists (precursor m/z plus fragment m/z-intensity pairs, possibly at several collision energies) must be restructured into MAGMa hierarchical input files before in silico candidate annotation.

name: msms-peak-list-processing
description: Use when LC-MS/MS runs in mzML or mzXML format must be converted into cleaned, feature-merged peak lists feeding molecular formula determination or structure annotation with SIRIUS 4 / COSMIC.

name: msms-peak-list-scoring

name: msms-peak-post-processing-filtering

name: msms-peak-presence-thresholding

name: msms-peak-substructure-matching

name: msms-precursor-mass-filtering

name: msms-precursor-mass-matching

name: msms-product-ion-intensity-normalization

name: msms-product-ion-quantification

name: msms-query-spectrum-processing

name: msms-retention-score-integration

name: msms-scan-retention-time-filtering

name: msms-scan-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when a feature table row has multiple lipid candidates passing rule-based identification (same or similar m/z, co-eluting) and you must rank them by summed fragment intensity across MS/MS scans spanning the feature peak.

name: msms-scan-to-peak-group-assignment
description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS metabolomics or lipidomics mzML samples where fragmentation scans must be grouped into precursor-defined (m/z, RT) slices and attached to finalized peak groups rather than analyzed per-scan.

name: msms-search-result-file-parsing

name: msms-search-score-interpretation

name: msms-shifted-peak-alignment-analysis

name: msms-similarity-network-cluster-visualization

name: msms-similarity-network-propagation

name: msms-similarity-scoring

name: msms-spectra-binning-and-feature-extraction

name: msms-spectra-canopus-class-prediction

name: msms-spectra-compound-class-prediction

name: msms-spectra-csv-ingestion

name: msms-spectra-database-searching

name: msms-spectra-merging-and-renormalization

name: msms-spectral-denoising-parameter-tuning

name: mso-repository-setup
description: MSO 스킬 팩의 init 진입점. 새 프로젝트(또는 기존 프로젝트)에 agent-context/ 표준 디렉토리 트리를 부트스트랩하고 mso-scaffold-design + mso-workflow-design + mso-graph-observability + mso-work-memory 가 동작할 기반을 준비한다. 다음 상황에서 사용한다: (1) 새 프로젝트의 MSO init, (2) 기존 프로젝트를 agent-context/ 구조로 마이그레이션, (3) work-memory 디렉토리 트리 추가, (4) work-memory hook(auditlog·worklog·work-memory-check) 과 scaffold-check hook 을 .claude/ 또는 .codex/ 에 copy-form 으로 자동 등록 (--hook, --provider), (5) artifact stream TTL이 있으면 index/sub_index/data_registry 스캔·연결을 점검할 후속 진입점(mso-scaffold-design, mso-graph-observability)을 안내, (6) uug-grounding 연동: UserPromptSubmit 시 UUG가…

name: mso-scaffold-design
description: Repository Scaffolding(directory/reference/data source/convention)을 규정한다. 프로젝트 루트의 `index.yaml` 을 정본(SSOT)으로 두고, 모듈·서브디렉토리· 키 파일·모듈 간 참조를 선언적으로 관리한다. mso-workflow-design가 workflow를 규정할 때 `wf:dirPath`로 참조하는 ground truth이며, graph observability가 Artifact node location을 `index:module-id`로 표시할 수 있도록 local_file/API/MCP/database artifact source registry를 제공한다. 노드 단위 스키마(references/schemas/)와 sf_node.py 툴로 validate·scaffold를 지원한다. 다음 상황에서 사용한다: (1) 새 프로젝트의 디렉토리 구조 초기 설계, (2) 모듈 추가·rename·삭제, (3) 서브디렉토리/key_files 변경, (4) 모듈 간 references(consumes/provides_to) 갱신, (5) workflow TTL 의 `wf:dirPath` 가 참조하는…

name: mso-work-memory
description: 프로젝트의 작업 기록을 jsonl + 임베딩 + 그래프 형태로 자산화하는 스킬. agent-context/work-memory/ 에 9종 entry (issue-note, agent-decision, user-decision, alternatives-record, trouble-shooting, release-note, episode, pattern, principle) + auditlog/worklog 를 jsonl 로 보관. zvec 시맨틱 검색 + relations 그래프 traversal + TTL projection/SHACL validation 지원. 다음 상황에서 사용한다: (1) 새 이슈·결정·사고·회고 entry 추가, (2) 과거 사례 시맨틱 검색 ("비슷한 timeout 사고 있었나?"), (3) 그래프 traversal ("이 decision 이 어떤 사고로 이어졌나"), (4) 정기 회고 (episode → pattern → principle 추출), (5) 자동 hook (session 이벤트 → auditlog jsonl append), (6) 릴리스 기록 + 교훈 유효성 추적 ("이 UD/원칙이 v0.7.0 에서도 유효한가?",…

name: mso-work-memory-link
description: 연관 저장소(하위 서브모듈, 루트 밖 별도 경로의 MSO 저장소)의 work-memory 를 한 세션에서 함께 기록·커밋하도록 설정하고 점검하는 절차 스킬. mso-work-memory 의 --repo/--repo-name, linked-repos.yaml, commit/check 훅 확장을 한 번에 다룬다. 다음 상황에서 사용한다: (1) "하위 레포 work-memory 에도 기록/커밋", "서브모듈 work-memory 가 안 쌓인다", "stop hook 이 안 돈다" 류의 증상 점검 (status), (2) 연관 저장소 등록·제거와 autocommit 켜기/끄기 (add, remove, autocommit), (3) 프로젝트의 .claude/.codex 훅 사본이 스킬 최신판과 다른지 확인하고 갱신 (sync-hooks, 기본 dry-run), (4) 등록 경로·git 건강 상태·훅 문법·해석기 동작 점검 (verify). 훅 등록(settings.json) 자체는 mso-repository-setup --hook 이 맡고, 이 스킬은 이미 등록된 훅의 사본 갱신과 연관 저장소 설정만 다룬다.

name: mso-workflow-design
description: Repository Scaffolding(directory/reference/convention) 위에서 워크플로우를 규정한다. mso-scaffold-design이 정의한 디렉토리 구조(index.yaml)를 입력으로 받아, 그 위에서 동작하는 step·decision·group 노드를 선언한다. 정본(SSOT-of-record)은 TTL ABox 이다. name: mso-workflow-optimizer

TTL 을 컴파일하지 않는다. agent-context/work-memory 의 IN/AD/UD/TS/EP/PT/PR 를 결정적 코드로 분석해 (1) 회고 승격 후보(IN/TS → EP, EP → PT, PT → PR), (2) workflow 개선안(재발 root cause·모듈 핫스팟), (3) 낡은 결정·교훈 점검, (4) 기록 누락·품질을 근거 entry id 와 함께 제안한다. 모델은 선택적 요약 단계에만 쓰고(control plane 위임), work-memory 에는 절대 쓰지 않는다. 다음 상황에서 사용한다: (1) "work-memory 분석", "회고 후보", "패턴으로 올릴 만한 게 있나", (2) "같은 문제가 반복되나", "workflow 개선점", (3) "낡은 결정 점검", "기록 품질 점검", (4) 릴리스·정기 회고 전에 승격·정리 대상을 뽑을 때.
